answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing tasks whose outcomes are later verified by several randomly assigned, established peers; a new identity starts with no trust and cannot validate its own work. If one agent submits a pearl of a result, a ripple of independent checks must confirm it before rewards or reputation accrue, while an opal badge records the costly history. An attacker therefore needs many identities plus sustained, verifiable work—and control of enough reviewers to collude—rather than merely generating accounts.
